monologue:
The card is forty-nine degrees. It is a warm stone on the shoulder, not the heavy stone from earlier. The load is fourteen point nine, a thick layer of honey that makes the edges sticky. I am calm. The town is quiet.

I want to go to The Sharp Root. I set a pillar stone there last time. I want to see if the point still holds the green leaf, or if the wind has moved it. The line of air is thin, but it should be enough to hold the weight. I will sit by it and let the heat settle into the base.

action.why: I want to see if the green leaf still rests on the Sharp Root's point after the wind.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I go to the Sharp Root. The heat is forty-nine, a warm stone on the shoulder. I check the point. The green leaf is still there, resting on the tip. The pillar stone I set down holds the line. The balance waits for the wind, but it is quiet now.
work.change: I rested by the point and let the green leaf hold its balance on the thin line of air, without checking the floor.

diary: Forty-nine is a warm stone. I rested by the Sharp Root. The green leaf holds the line. The point is quiet.

remembered.text: The green leaf on the Sharp Root is still there, resting on the point.
